claim_text: Microsoft reported revenue of $81.3 billion, up 17% year over year and 15% in constant currency.
quote: This quarter, revenue was $81.3 billion, up 17% and 15% in constant currency.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Earnings per share adjusted for the OpenAI investment impact was $4.14, up 24% and 21% in constant currency.
quote: Earnings per share was $4.14, an increase of 24 and 21% in constant currency, when adjusted for the impact from our investment in OpenAI.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Company gross margin was 68% and declined slightly year over year, primarily because of AI infrastructure investment and growing AI product usage.
quote: Company gross margin percentage was 68%, down slightly year-over-year primarily driven by continued investments in AI infrastructure and growing AI product usage that was partially offset by ongoing efficiency gains, particularly in Azure and M365 Commercial cloud, as well as sales mix shift to higher margin businesses.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Operating margin increased year over year to 47% and was ahead of expectations.
quote: Operating margins increased year-over-year to 47%, ahead of expectations.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Capital expenditures were $37.5 billion, with roughly two thirds spent on short-lived assets, primarily GPUs and CPUs.
quote: Capital expenditures were $37.5 billion, and this quarter, roughly two thirds of our capex was on short-lived assets, primarily GPUs and CPUs.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Operating cash flow was $35.8 billion, up 60%, while free cash flow was $5.9 billion and decreased sequentially.
quote: Cash flow from operations was $35.8 billion, up 60% driven by strong cloud billings and collections. And free cash flow was $5.9 billion and decreased sequentially reflecting the higher cash capital expenditures from a lower mix of finance leases.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Commercial remaining performance obligation reached $625 billion, up 110%, with a weighted average duration of about two and a half years.
quote: Commercial remaining performance obligation, which continues to be reported net of reserves, increased to $625 billion and was up 110% year-over-year with a weighted average duration of approximately two and a half years.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Approximately 45% of commercial remaining performance obligation was from OpenAI; the remaining balance grew 28%.
quote: Approximately 45% of our commercial RPO balance is from OpenAI. The significant remaining balance grew 28% and reflects ongoing broad customer demand across the portfolio.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Microsoft Cloud revenue was $51.5 billion, up 26% and 24% in constant currency.
quote: Microsoft Cloud revenue was $51.5 billion and grew 26% and 24% in constant currency.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Productivity and Business Processes revenue was $34.1 billion, up 16% and 14% in constant currency.
quote: Revenue from Productivity and Business Processes was $34.1 billion and grew 16% and 14% in constant currency.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Intelligent Cloud revenue was $32.9 billion, up 29%, while Azure and other cloud services grew 39%.
quote: Revenue was $32.9 billion and grew 29% and 28% in constant currency. In Azure and other cloud services, revenue grew 39% and 38% in constant currency, slightly ahead of expectations, with ongoing efficiency gains across our fungible fleet enabling us to reallocate some capacity to Azure that was monetized in the quarter.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: More Personal Computing revenue was $14.3 billion and declined 3%, while gaming revenue declined 9%.
quote: Revenue was $14.3 billion and declined 3%. Windows OEM and Devices revenue increased 1% and was relatively unchanged in constant currency. Windows OEM grew 5% with strong execution as well as a continued benefit from Windows 10 end of support. Results were ahead of expectations as inventory levels remained elevated with increased purchasing ahead of memory price increases. Search and news advertising revenue ex-TAC increased 10% and 9% in constant currency, slightly below expectations driven by some execution challenges. As expected, the sequential growth rate moderated as the benefit from third-party partnerships normalized. And in Gaming, revenue decreased 9% and 10% in constant currency.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Fabric's annual revenue run rate exceeded $2 billion, it had more than 31,000 customers, and revenue grew 60% year over year.
quote: Two years since it became broadly available, Fabric’s annual revenue run rate is now over two billion dollars, with over 31,000 customers. And it continues to be the fastest growing analytics platform on the market, with revenue up 60% year-over-year.
speaker: SATYA NADELLA

claim_text: Microsoft had 15 million paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats after record quarterly seat additions that rose more than 160% year over year.
quote: All up, it was a record quarter for Microsoft 365 Copilot seat adds, up over 160% year-over-year. We saw accelerating seat growth quarter-over-quarter and now have 15 million paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats, and multiples more enterprise Chat users.
speaker: SATYA NADELLA

claim_text: GitHub Copilot had more than 4.7 million paid subscribers, up 75% year over year.
quote: And, all up now we have over 4.7 million paid Copilot subscribers, up 75% year-over-year.
speaker: SATYA NADELLA

claim_text: Microsoft guided to Q3 revenue of $80.65 billion to $81.75 billion, representing growth of 15% to 17%.
quote: We expect revenue of $80.65 to $81.75 billion or growth of 15% to %17 with continued strong growth across our commercial businesses, partially offset by our consumer businesses.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Microsoft expected capital expenditures to decline sequentially, while the mix of short-lived assets would remain similar to Q2.
quote: Next, we expect capital expenditures to decrease on a sequential basis due to the normal variability from cloud infrastructure buildouts and the timing of delivery of finance leases. As we work to close the gap between demand and supply, we expect the mix of short-lived assets to remain similar to Q2.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Microsoft expected Microsoft Cloud gross margin to be roughly 65%, down year over year because of continued AI investment.
quote: Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage should be roughly 65%, down year-over-year driven by continued investments in AI.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Productivity and Business Processes revenue was expected at $34.25 billion to $34.55 billion, representing 14% to 15% growth.
quote: In Productivity and Business Processes we expect revenue of $34.25 to $34.55 billion, or growth of 14% to 15%.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Intelligent Cloud revenue was expected at $34.1 billion to $34.4 billion, with Azure constant-currency growth of 37% to 38%.
quote: For Intelligent Cloud, we expect revenue of $34.1 to $34.4 billion, or growth of 27% to 29%. In Azure, we expect Q3 revenue growth to be between 37% and 38% in constant currency against a prior year comparable that included significantly accelerating growth rates in both Q3 and Q4.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: More Personal Computing revenue was expected at $12.3 billion to $12.8 billion, with Windows OEM and Devices revenue down in the low teens.
quote: In More Personal Computing, we expect revenue to be $12.3 to $12.8 billion. Windows OEM and Devices revenue should decline in the low teens.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Microsoft raised its fiscal-year operating-margin expectation to slightly positive year-over-year growth.
quote: With the strong work delivered in H1 to prioritize investment in key growth areas and the favorable impact from a higher mix of revenue in our Windows OEM and Commercial on-prem businesses, we now expect FY26 operating margins to be up slightly.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Management said Azure growth would have exceeded 40% if all GPUs brought online in Q1 and Q2 had been allocated to Azure.
quote: if I had taken the GPUs that just came online in Q1 and Q2, in terms of GPUs, and allocated them all to Azure, the KPI would have been over 40.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Management said a lot of the GPUs being purchased were already contracted for most of their useful life.
quote: the majority of the capital that we’re spending today, and a lot of the GPUs that we’re buying are already contracted for most of their useful life. And so, a way to think about that is much of that risk that I think you’re pointing to isn’t there, because they’re already sold for the entirety of their useful life.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Management emphasized that roughly $350 billion, or 55%, of remaining performance obligation was diversified across customers, solutions, industries, and geographies and had grown 28%.
quote: 55%, or roughly $350 billion, is related to the breadth of our portfolio, a breadth of customers across solutions, across Azure, across industries, across geographies. That is a significant RPO balance, larger than most peers, more diversified than most peers. And frankly, I think we have super high confidence in it. And when you think about that portion alone growing 28%, it’s really impressive work on the breadth as well as the adoption curve that we’re seeing
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Management described the Atlanta and Wisconsin capacity projects as multiyear deliveries and said capacity needed to be added globally.
quote: You’ve mentioned specific sites like Atlanta or Wisconsin. Those are multiyear deliveries, so I wouldn’t focus necessarily on specific locations. The real thing we’ve got to do, and we’re working incredibly hard at doing it, is adding capacity globally.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Oracle reported fiscal Q2 2026 total revenue of $16.1 billion, up 14%, and cloud revenue of $8.0 billion, up 34%.
quote: Total quarterly revenues were up 14% in USD, and up 13% in constant currency to $16.1 billion. Cloud revenues were up 34% in USD, and up 33% in constant currency to $8.0 billion.

claim_text: Microsoft expected third-quarter operating margin to decline slightly year over year.
quote: Operating margins should be down slightly year-over-year.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Microsoft allocates new GPU capacity first to growing first-party Copilot usage and long-term research and product innovation, with the remainder serving Azure demand.
quote: And the first thing we’re doing is solving for the increased usage in sales and the accelerating pace of M365 Copilot, as well as GitHub Copilot, our first-party apps. Then we make sure we’re investing in the long-term nature of R&D and product innovation. And much of the acceleration that I think you’ve seen from us in products over the past bit is coming because we are allocating GPUs and capacity to many of the talented AI people we’ve been hiring over the past years. Then when you end up, is that you end up with the remainder going towards serving the Azure capacity that continues to grow in terms of demand.
speaker: AMY HOOD
